tier_reason: Public third-party shootout (djkoloski/rust_serialization_benchmark: benches/bench.rs, src/bench_bilrost.rs vs src/bench_prost.rs) with prost in the same table; README states rustc 1.100.0-nightly (a36d05efa 2026-09-09), LLVM 23.1.1, CPU AMD EPYC 9V74, and Cargo.toml [profile.bench] lto=true (release-level opt). All code, compiler, flags and CPU are stated, so A holds.

corrections.claimed_speedup: log dataset: bilrost 0.1016.1 serialize 396.57 us (encode) / 300.26 us (prepend) vs prost 0.14.4 731.23 us (encode only) / 1.8883 ms (populate + encode): ~2.4x faster vs encode-only, ~6.3x vs populate+encode (derived from page data). Deserialize bilrost 2.1234 ms vs prost 2.6802 ms (decode) / 2.7061 ms (decode + convert): ~1.26x faster (derived from page data).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: rustc 1.100.0-nightly (a36d05efa 2026-09-09), LLVM 23.1.1; Criterion via cargo bench, [profile.bench] lto = true
corrections.caveats: Speedup varies by dataset and by which prost variant is compared: the 6.3x serialize figure is vs prost populate+encode (conversion from the native struct included); vs prost encode-only it is ~2.4x. On 'mesh' bilrost is still ahead (encode 4.2651 ms vs prost encode 5.8939 ms; deserialize 5.8287 ms vs 10.253 ms), so the earlier note that it is not clearly ahead there was wrong. bilrost's author (mumbleskates) is listed as a maintainer of the benchmark suite. Harvested from a shootout, not bilrost's own README.

notes: Numbers match bilrost's and prost's rows on the log table (last updated 2026-09-10). Default-branch last commit is 2026-08-14 (repo pushed_at 2026-09-21 is likely another branch). License Apache-2.0, 47 stars, not fork/archived.

tier_reason: Same public shootout (djkoloski/rust_serialization_benchmark: benches/bench.rs, src/bench_minicbor.rs vs src/bench_rmp_serde.rs) with rmp-serde (MessagePack) and ciborium (CBOR) in the same table; rustc 1.100.0-nightly/LLVM 23.1.1, [profile.bench] lto=true, and CPU AMD EPYC 9V74 are all stated, so A holds.

corrections.claimed_speedup: log dataset: minicbor 2.3.0 serialize 405.77 us vs rmp-serde 1.3.1 1.3179 ms (~3.2x faster, derived from page data); deserialize 2.3448 ms vs 2.3829 ms (on par). Vs prost 0.14.4: ~1.8x vs encode-only 731.23 us, ~4.7x vs populate+encode 1.8883 ms (derived). Vs the common serde CBOR crate ciborium 0.2.2: serialize 3.3751 ms (~8.3x) and deserialize 10.862 ms (~4.6x) (derived from page data).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: rustc 1.100.0-nightly (a36d05efa 2026-09-09), LLVM 23.1.1; Criterion via cargo bench, [profile.bench] lto = true
corrections.caveats: Serialize-only win over MessagePack's rmp-serde: deserialize is on par on log and slightly slower on mesh (9.4268 vs 9.2506 ms) and minecraft_savedata (2.6924 vs 2.3727 ms). Other MessagePack crates in the same table (msgpacker 266.04 us, zerompk 269.23 us serialize; 2.0663 / 1.8129 ms deserialize) beat minicbor, so it is faster than the incumbent rmp-serde, not than MessagePack in general. Its clearest win is over ciborium (CBOR). Output is smaller than ciborium's (817830 vs 1407835 bytes on log), so the encodings differ. corrections.claimed_speedup: log dataset: nanoserde 0.2.1 serialize 190.59 us vs prost 0.14.4 731.23 us encode-only (~3.8x) / 1.8883 ms populate+encode (~9.9x); deserialize 1.6898 ms vs prost decode 2.6802 ms (~1.6x) (ratios derived from page data). It also beats prost on the other datasets, e.g. mesh deserialize 824.47 us vs 10.253 ms.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: rustc 1.100.0-nightly (a36d05efa 2026-09-09), LLVM 23.1.1; Criterion via cargo bench, [profile.bench] lto = true
corrections.caveats: The 9.9x serialize figure is vs prost populate+encode; vs prost encode-only it is ~3.8x. nanoserde's binary output size on log (1045784 bytes) matches wincode and bin-proto, not borsh (885780). Faster plain struct-layout encoders exist in the same table (wincode 137.05 us serialize / 1.4166 ms deserialize on log). This is a no-schema struct encoding, not a distinct schema language.
